php.comment: PHP source/sink/sanitizer model for the line/statement recognizer (core/taint/engine/extract_php.go). java.comment: Java source/sink/sanitizer model for the lexctx line/statement recognizer (no CGo tree-sitter). Sinks come in two shapes, matched via the engine's suffixKeys fallback: (1) package/class-qualified calls matched on the full dotted chain (Files.readAllBytes, ObjectInputStream.readObject), and (2) methods on a value whose receiver name varies — matched by METHOD-NAME suffix (.executeQuery, .println, .exec, .start). rust.comment: Rust source/sink/sanitizer model. Calls are matched in the extractor's NORMALIZED dotted form: the Rust line recognizer rewrites the `::` path separator to `.` and drops the `!` on macro invocations, so `std::env::var` is keyed `env.var`, `Command::new` is `Command.new`, and `sqlx::query!` is `sqlx.query`. Method calls whose receiver varies (`.arg`/`.args` on a Command builder, `.bind` on a query) are matched on the bare method suffix via the engine's suffixKeys fallback. Rust recognition is COARSER than Python/JS/Go (no real parser — only Go gets go/ast): ownership/moves, Result/`?` unwrapping, iterator chains, and macro expansion are invisible to the recognizer, so Rust recall is expected to be the lowest of the supported languages. See testdata/precision-suite-rust/README.md for the measured gaps. The web-extractor sources (`web.Query`/`web.Form`/`web.Json`/`web.Path` for actix, bare `Query`/`Form`/`Json`/`Path` for axum) are matched not only as constructor calls but also as PARAMETER TYPES: extract_rust.go seeds a function parameter whose type is one of these extractors as tainted-on-entry (via a synthetic `binding = <source>()` statement), because a `web::Query<Params>` handler argument is untrusted input even though it never appears as a source call.

cpp.comment: C/C++ taint model: INJECTION-CLASS dataflow only (command injection, path traversal, format string, SSRF, SQLi). Memory-safety bugs (buffer overflow strcpy/strcat/sprintf/gets -> CWE-120/787, use-after-free, OOB) are a DIFFERENT analysis than source->sink taint and are OUT OF SCOPE for this engine — see testdata/precision-suite-cpp/README.md. Call keys are the short/bare form; the extractor normalizes C++ `::` to `.` and the engine suffix-matches, so `system` matches `std::system` and `getenv` matches `std::getenv`.

perl.comment: Perl source/sink/sanitizer model for the line/statement recognizer (core/taint/engine/extract_perl.go). The `$`/`@`/`%` sigils are stripped during normalization, so `$ENV{X}` reads source `ENV`, `@ARGV` reads `ARGV`, and `$q->param` normalizes to the dotted chain `q.param` matched by the `.param` suffix. Backtick and qx command literals are modeled as a synthetic `` ` `` command-injection sink. Perl is recognized pragmatically (no interpreter), so recall is moderate by design; precision is held >= 0.90. Rule IDs mirror the shared TAINT-00x space.

objc.comment: Objective-C / Objective-C++ taint model for the line/statement recognizer (core/taint/engine/extract_objc.go). Bracket message sends `[recv selector:arg ...]` are rewritten to dotted calls `recv.selector(arg, ...)` before recognition, so every sink/source/sanitizer below is keyed on the SELECTOR SUFFIX (matched by the engine's dotted-suffix fallback): `[db executeQuery:sql]` keys on `executeQuery`, `[NSURLSession dataTaskWithURL:u]` on `dataTaskWithURL`, `[task launch]` on `launch`. C runtime calls (`system`, `popen`, `exec*`, `fopen`, `sqlite3_*`) key on their bare name. Like the C/C++ block this is INJECTION-CLASS dataflow only; memory-safety bugs are a different analysis and out of scope. See testdata/precision-suite-objc/README.md.

powershell.comment: PowerShell source/sink/sanitizer model for the line/statement recognizer (core/taint/engine/extract_powershell.go). PowerShell shapes are normalized before recognition: the `$` variable sigil is stripped (like PHP), the static-member `::` becomes `.` with the `[Namespace.Type]` accelerator unwrapped (so `[IO.File]::ReadAllText` keys as `IO.File.ReadAllText`, matched by the `.ReadAllText` suffix), a `[int]`/`[long]` cast becomes an `int(...)`/`long(...)` sanitizer call, the `$env:` provider becomes a bare `env` read, and — CRUCIALLY — a cmdlet's `Verb-Noun` hyphen is normalized to an UNDERSCORE (`Invoke-Expression` -> `Invoke_Expression`) because the shared identifier scanner treats `-` as an operator. Every hyphenated cmdlet key below therefore uses the underscore form. Paren-less cmdlet calls (`Get-Content $p`) are wrapped into `Get_Content($p)`, and the call operator `& $cmd` is modeled as the synthetic sink `InvokeOperator`. Rule IDs mirror the shared TAINT-00x space. PowerShell recall is moderate (pipelines, splatting, and paren-less pipeline arguments are only partially modeled) — see testdata/precision-suite-powershell/README.md.

groovy.comment: Groovy source/sink/sanitizer model for the lexctx line/statement recognizer (no CGo parser). Groovy runs on the JVM, so it shares much of Java's dangerous-API surface, but its idioms differ: command execution is the String receiver method "cmd".execute() (keyed on the .execute method suffix), Jenkins pipeline steps sh/bat run shell commands, and SQL uses groovy.sql.Sql (rows/executeQuery/firstRow/eachRow). GString interpolation "...${x}..." is the dominant injection carrier; lexctx emits the ${} hole as CODE so the tainted expression is visible. Sinks are matched via the engine's suffixKeys fallback: package/class-qualified calls on the full chain (Eval.me, GroovyShell.evaluate) and value-method calls by METHOD-NAME suffix (.execute, .rows, .text). Method-suffix matching is imprecise on purpose (AST-only); the corpus README records the resulting honest FNs (closure/DSL laundering the flat recognizer cannot follow). See core/taint/engine/extract_groovy.go.
